Unlike SLAM-based methods such as GS-SLAM or RTG-SLAM that require spatial and temporal continuity and often depth priors, On-the-Fly GS handles discrete images captured in an arbitrary manner without spatiotemporal continuity, relying only on a certain degree of overlap with previously registered images [S1].

The claim is explicitly stated in the provided source text. Specifically, Source [S1] passages contain the sentence: 'In contrast, our On-the-Fly GS, which can deal with images captured in an arbitrary way without spatiotemporal continuity, employs a progressive framework for near realtime 3DGS training. It only requires that the newly fly-in image has a certain degree of overlap with all previously registered images, and does not rely on depth priors for 3DGS field expansion.' Additionally, the notes for Source [S1] include the exact phrasing: 'Unlike SLAM-based methods (e.g., GS-SLAM, RTG-SLAM) that require spatial and temporal continuity and often depth priors, On-the-Fly GS handles discrete images captured in an arbitrary manner without spatiotemporal continuity, relying only on a certain degree of overlap with previously registered images.' Therefore, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
